paragraphs.text: Cut MCP token cost in DSH (DeepSeek Harness): send tool definitions as a compact index and load full
schemas on demand, with the tool list stable so the prompt cache keeps working.
# dsh-tool-index
**75 MCP tools connected, one small task: 183,274 tokens without this plugin, 79,838 with it — 56% l
CP tools connected, one small task: 183,274 tokens without this plugin, 79,838 with it — 56% less.**
`dsh-tool-index` sends your MCP tool definitions as a compact index and loads full schemas only when
the model asks for them. The tool list itself never changes mid-session, so your prompt cache keeps
l asks for them. The tool list itself never changes mid-session, so your prompt cache keeps working.
A plugin for DSH. Built on DeepSeek Harness; not an official DeepSeek project.
## The problem
Every tool definition is sent again on every model request. Connect a few MCP servers and an agent c
arries hundreds of definitions it never uses: thousands of tokens on every step, and a model that pi
cks tools worse because it has too many to choose from.
## What it does
`dsh-tool-index` sends those tools as a short index instead: each tool's **name, parameters and one-
line summary**, grouped by server. When the model needs one, it reads the full details with `tool_de
tails` and runs it with `call_tool`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Fewer tokens on every request.** The MCP tools cost about 88% less per request.
- **The prompt c
ache keeps working.** The tool list stays the same for the whole session, so loading a tool never fo

rces the provider to re-read the conversation at full price.
- **The model doesn't miss tools.** Eve
ry tool is always named in the index, and a wrong name (a typo, a missing `mcp__server__` prefix) ge

ts the closest real names back.
- **Nothing is bypassed.** Permission policies, approvals and hooks
still see the real tool and its arguments.
## Does it save tokens?
Yes. One small task, three runs per cell, with real MCP servers:
| Model | Without the plugin | With it | Change |

| DeepSeek deepseek-flash, 25 MCP tools | 80,777 | 58,864 | **-27%** |
| DeepSeek deepseek-flash, 75

MCP tools | 183,274 | 79,838 | **-56%** |
| Claude claude-haiku-5-5, 25 MCP tools | 110,598 | 94,42
And over a 5-message conversation in one session (DeepSeek, two of the messages need no tools):
| Servers | Without the plugin | With it | Change |
Tokens summed over every model step. Every run finished its task with and without the plugin. The mo
re tools you connect, the more it saves.
Reproduce them yourself with `e2e/run.sh`.
## Install
On npm as `dsh-tool-index` — DSH fetches it for you, so there is no `npm install` step.
As a bundle in a profile:

## Configuration
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A patch replaces a row's whole `config`, so restate every key you set.
With fewer than `minTools` matching tools nothing changes: a handful of definitions costs less than
n `minTools` matching tools nothing changes: a handful of definitions costs less than an extra step.
Keep tools the agent uses on most turns out of the index with `exclude` or `alwaysLoad`.
This plugin is for MCP tools. `match` takes name prefixes, but deferring your harness's own core too
ls (`read`, `bash` and the like) will make the agent worse, not cheaper: it needs them on almost eve
ry turn, and there is no guard against it.
## Trade-offs
- **Sometimes one extra step** (`tool_details`) before a deferred tool is first used in a conversati

on.
- **Arguments are checked by the tool, not by the provider.** A wrong argument comes back as the

tool's own error.
- **UIs show `call_tool`** as the outer step, with the real tool inside it.
## Compatibility

- **Native tool calls:** the mode the plugin is built for.
- **PTC mode** (`run_code`): the plugin s
teps aside for those agents and adds nothing to their requests. In PTC mode the model calls tools fr

om code, and DSH already lists every tool for that code.
- **Sub-agents and structured-output childr
en:** each agent gets its own index of its own tools. A child's `structured_output` tool stays a nor
h agent gets its own index of its own tools. A child's `structured_output` tool stays a normal tool.
Written for DSH 0.2.x. DSH is pre-1.0, so its plugin interfaces can change between releases.
## How it works
- docs/how-it-works.md — the index, `tool_details`, `call_tool`, and why the tool list stays fixed.
- docs/name-matching.md — how a wrong tool name is matched to the closest real one.
